original_context_note: Compared target-selection.json/full_target and problem.md:44–122 with spec.full_target (exact retained text), spec.conclusion/P, H001–H003 and D001–D012. The ambient parameters are exactly real T,gamma,R; their original ranges are retained as H. The original real/mean-zero/H^gamma/radius datum conditions and positive-integer timestep restriction are fully retained under P's universal quantifiers, allowing C,tau0 to be chosen first uniformly on the ball. R014 introduces and discharges these local conditions; none has been converted into an extra trusted H. All original H are used. D001–D008 preserve the normalized 2*pi torus, Fourier and Sobolev completions, reality, zero modes, Airy sign, projections and inverse derivatives. D009–D010 reproduce every coefficient and endpoint in the selected fixed scheme, including S_(s-tau), tau/9, -1/54 and -1/(27tau); D011 defines positive-tau iterates and specializes to T/L under H001. Their L2 well-definedness and continuity are proved in N005; no property is supplied by definition. D012 is a solution convention/relationship, with existence proved in N001 rather than assumed. D013–D023 preserve the covariance, cubic Fourier remainder, third frequency, continuous operators, pstar, exact-data stage and all interpolation/residual formulas from problem.md:123–540. The sole guarded definition D022 retains the original agamma piecewise formula with requires H002, now a direct input at every dependent use. Local D023 formulas may be instantiated at arbitrary smooth step states; global continuity and numerical endpoint agreement are proved in N008. Read actual primary texts: E001 uses the exact 42-page arXiv:0910.1389v2, its Section 3 conventions and Theorems 4.2–4.3,5.1,6.3–6.5; E002–E005 use the cited 50-page Li–Wu FoCM-3.pdf with complete Proposition 3.4, Lemma 7.2, product inequalities and update/remainder identities in context. Author/title/version/page and DOI metadata were checked; Google access failures are preserved, but the adequate author primary PDF was obtained, so there is no primary-source deferral. E001's opposite dispersive sign and homogeneous norm conversion are proved in R001; Li–Wu's sqrt(2*pi) norm conversions are proved in R006–R007; R008 checks the full update identity. Neither published logarithmic convergence nor the target theorem is imported. The graph has five external roots, thirteen uniquely produced internal results and one target; its actual AND edges are acyclic and all retained nodes lie in P's backward closure. The partition follows separate coherent tasks for flow normalization, covariance/majorants, dyadic summation, mixed remainder, elementary operators, each source bridge, exact interpolation, stages, defect, residual, restarted stability, bootstrap and density. R012 is the largest task because its normal-form signs, output split and actual forcing estimate form one tightly connected local implication; its five S phases keep their scopes distinct. This preserves the supplied proof route and every calculation, limiting argument and intermediate bound needed by Theorem 1. The Section 5 numerical experiments, empirical tables/figures and implementation campaign are omitted: they are independent illustrations explicitly excluded from the analytic conclusion by the supplied text, and no theorem step depends on them. Routine analytic background is used with explicit conditions and displayed local justifications, without pretending to native Mathlib certification. I actually read all fourteen current own packets, including changed views after repairs, using only each packet's direct inputs as conditional premises. These are same-author checks under yui-nl0-audit-a-2, not independent Audit A or mathematical certification by the structural validator.

output_notes.note: R001/S001–S004 exports actual existence, regularity, smoothness and the uniform H^gamma bound for the original-sign equation, together with the full two-flow L2 estimate needed by R014. Norms and equation sign are identified explicitly.

R002/S001 gives both covariance ratios and both tau-phase bounds including zero phases; S002–S003 give the two separate 1/N3 majorants and N1<=3N2 under precisely the nonzero zero-sum conditions used in R004.

R003/S001–S003 gives the unrestricted nonnegative ell2 four-linear inequality, uniform constant and arbitrary-subset variant, with the infinite sum understood as a positive supremum. No finite-support condition escapes the proof.

R004/S001–S003 proves every 0<=sigma<=1 trilinear bound, the extension, arbitrary-modulus multiplier and resonant restrictions. S004 exports the numerical-state estimate under only L2 proximity to a bounded H^gamma comparison state.

R005 exports each elementary operator/product estimate, exact normal-form coefficient and both endpoints, the Cop substitution identity, and fixed-positive-tau scheme continuity/preservation. These are the actual statements consumed downstream, rather than references to an original equation number.

R006 exports the full dynamic Cop estimate with any negative-norm slot and the full static H^sigma estimate, on all nonnegative intervals of length <=1 with source-independent interval location. Xnorm and normalized spaces are defined in its packet.

R007 exports the chosen agamma product inequality and both stage bounds, with full step, comparison-state and exponent domains and all constant dependencies. H002 supplies the D022 guard at every actual use.

R008 exports the exact update, both interpolation endpoint equalities, continuity/piecewise smoothness, mean-zero properties and the full Y_n' and residual/V' identities. Later units do not need the source's derivation body.

R009 exports all H^1, H^agamma, L2 and Xnorm stage bounds, the nonlinear square bound, Q_n/W_n size and inverse-derivative product bound with the complete comparison-state premises and support uniformity.

R010 exports the two inverse-derivative bounds, strong L2, Xnorm and small H^(-pstar) bounds. Its statement repeats every conditional step hypothesis, so the decisive tau*q_n smallness is available in R011–R012 without its producer body.

R011 exports the two step residual bounds and all interval residual/error/trajectory estimates, with a grid-start requirement, E_I<=1, h<=1 and permission for a partial last step. The sum has the required h+tau factor.

R012 exports the exact error identity, low/high output estimates and the entire absorbable recurrence for every threshold N>=2. It states every interval/bootstrap condition and the uniformity in restart, step and support needed for R013.

R013 exports one C,tau0 for all smooth data in the radius-R ball and all permitted positive integer step counts, for both interpolation and grid error. The quantifier order and constant dependence are uniform in higher Sobolev norms.

R014 proves exactly the selected uniform O(tau^gamma) grid estimate for every real mean-zero H^gamma datum in the radius ball and every permitted integer L. The frozen full_target is preserved byte for byte; D001–D012 preserve all domain, normalization, equation, exact-solution and unfiltered update formulas, including n=0 and n=L.
